entities.summary: Philastrius was a bishop in the early Christian Church who played a significant role in the development of Christianity during the 4th century. He was one of the bishops present at a synod held in Aquileia in 381, where the Nicene Creed was reaffirmed and the boundaries of orthodoxy were established. Philastrius's significance lies in his contributions to the shaping of Christian doctrine and practice, which had far-reaching consequences for the development of Western civilization. His legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the bishops' role in the Church and the ongoing relevance of the Nicene Creed. One striking statistic about Philastrius is that he was one of only a handful of bishops present at this synod who survived into old age, testifying to the enduring power of Christian faith and leadership.
